name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt the 2px focus ring at 7:1 contrast. It survives color inversion and reduced-motion modes without breaking, unlike the 3px ring which can blur into backgrounds. The trade-off is slightly less visual pop in ideal conditions, but that’s acceptable since the ring must work in worst-case scenarios.

name: Reader
text: The 2px ring at 7:1 still risks vanishing on monochrome displays where contrast collapses to near-zero—users lose the ring entirely. A 3px ring at 4.5:1 contrast survives monochrome and high-contrast modes without disappearing, trading some pop in ideal conditions for universal visibility. Test both on a monochrome monitor to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 3px focus ring at 4.5:1 contrast. It’s the only option that survives monochrome, high-contrast, and reduced-motion modes without vanishing—users must see the ring everywhere. The trade-off is slightly less visual pop in ideal conditions, but that’s irrelevant when the ring fails in critical scenarios.

name: Reader
text: A 3px ring at 4.5:1 still risks blending into backgrounds on some monochrome displays where contrast collapses—users lose the ring when the background turns pure white or black. The real fix is a 3px ring at 7:1 contrast with a 1px outer glow (white on dark, black on light) to guarantee visibility in all modes. Test both in monochrome, high-contrast, and reduced-motion modes to settle it.
